notes: cookingMethodFor() in source returns exactly ONE phrase per condition -- it has no professional/friendly/luxury tone parameter at all (that's a templateNlgProvider/hospitalityKnowledge distinction that applies elsewhere, not here). Per the requested schema shape (cooking_method_phrases {professional, friendly, luxury}) the single source phrase is repeated identically under all three tone keys below, flagged with fidelity_note: 'single-tone in source'.
cookingMethodFor() checks rules in order and returns on first match (if/else-if chain) -- 'match_priority' reflects that exact order.

Before any protein/texture/course check, cookingMethodFor() first tests CONDIMENT_RE = /\b(sauce|butter|dressing|dip|chutney|relish|glaze)\b/ against the lowercased item name; if it matches, the function returns '' immediately (no cooking-method line for condiments/enhancements), regardless of the item's own protein/course tags.

typical_sides for each protein come from aiService.js addFoodPairings()'s foodRules array, matched on dish-name/searchText regex (not directly on the protein tag) -- captured verbatim as 'dish_regex' + 'keywords' per protein below.

Not every protein has a dedicated foodRules entry: lamb and game share cookingMethodFor()'s grilling logic with beef but have NO separate foodRules side-dish entry in aiService.js (no /lamb/ or /game/ regex exists in foodRules) -- typical_sides is empty for those two, flagged explicitly rather than invented.
